name: Nuclear risk
value: No US–Russia treaty limits since 5 Feb
summary: No US–Russia arms limits since New START lapsed; Trump, Xi and Putin to meet on 19 Nov with nuclear arms on the agenda
state: New START expired on 5 Feb with no replacement; the five nuclear-weapon states held unpublicised talks in New York in early October, and China rejected trilateral arms talks on 16 Oct (Arms Control Association). China confirmed a Trump–Xi–Putin meeting in Shenzhen on 19 Nov, where nuclear arms control is expected to be discussed (UNN, 16 Nov). No nuclear test, alert-level change or threatened use was found as of 16 Nov, so Watch holds.
for_you: No change in UK government advice. Arms-control lapses raise long-run risk rather than immediate danger.

sources.title: Arms Control Association — Nuclear-weapon states consult as Trump talks denuclearization
UNN — China confirms Trump, Putin and Xi meeting on 19 November

why: Nuclear use anywhere would be a civilisational shock; arms-control treaties are weaker than at any time since the 1960s.
drivers: Threats in active wars, testing, doctrine changes, arms-control collapse, proliferation.

rubric.alert: A nuclear test, changes in deployment/alert levels, or threatened use in an active conflict.
rubric.watch: Explicit threats, unusual exercises, doctrine changes, or arms-control lapses without replacement.
rubric.normal: No explicit nuclear threats or tests; arms-control dialogue active.
